The GrowthCred field guide

Give AI context about your business.

Why does AI give you generic answers? Because it knows nothing about your business. A business brain fixes that. It's one document that says how your business works, so you brief AI the same way every time. It won't make every tool remember everything. It won't make every answer right. But it's where good answers start.

By Phila Ngwenya · Reviewed 20 September 2026

Write the facts once

Start with your services. Your ideal customers. The tasks that repeat. Your tone. The terms you've approved. Keep confirmed facts apart from ideas. Add a review date. And name the person who keeps it current.

Want a head start? Use my free Business Brain builder. Answer the questions, then copy or download your document. Check it before you use it. The builder puts your answers together. It doesn't check your facts.

A starting template

Copy these headings into a document. Keep the first version short. Short enough to check in five minutes.

  • Business: what we do, who we serve and where we operate.
  • Services: scope, exclusions and where approved pricing is stored.
  • Voice: a short example of writing we would actually send.
  • Workflow: inputs, steps, output and the person who approves it.
  • Rules: ask when information is missing; do not invent prices or commitments.
  • Maintenance: owner, review date and what has changed.

Try it on something small

Picture a made-up maintenance business. It needs a follow-up after a meeting. Give the AI a sample meeting note and your approved service description. Ask it to sum up what the customer needs, draft a short email and list anything it couldn't confirm.

Now do the same without the context. Compare them. Which is more accurate? Which sounds like you? Which took less fixing? You're after a repeatable improvement. Not just a longer answer.

Connect it carefully

Tools handle documents and instructions differently. Check the tool's current docs and account settings. Uploading a document once doesn't mean every chat, or every connected tool, can see it.

Keep passwords out of it. And any personal information you don't need. Practise with a made-up or redacted example. Agree who can see what before real client material goes in.

Keep it useful

Update it whenever your prices, services or terms change. Keep one short test task and rerun it after big changes. Does the AI keep getting something wrong? Fix the source and the workflow. Don't pile on instructions that contradict each other.

The brain is the start. A workflow you can trust also needs good inputs, a person checking and one place where the approved version lives.
